text: In Alaska, there is a town where almost everyone lives in one building.
Whittier. About two hundred and seventy people. One fourteen-story tower.
It was built for the army in the nineteen fifties. When the soldiers left, the town moved in.
Inside: the police station. The post office. A store. A clinic. A church.
The school is across the street, and the kids get there through an underground tunnel.
Because every winter, Whittier gets more than six metres of snow.
The only road into town? Another tunnel. One lane, shared with trains. And it closes at night.
Some people barely step outside all winter.
Here, you know everybody. And everybody knows you.
As one teacher put it: it's a community under one roof.
In Whittier, nobody is ever more than a few floors from a friend.
Most of us aren't that lucky. Our people are miles away, or busy, or asleep.
That's why we made Feeloy. Jenny is always one tap away, day or night.
